launchError: The launch data source is temporarily unavailable.
launchNotFound: GCAT has no matching launch record for this object yet.
launchStale: Showing the last saved launch details. The source is temporarily unavailable.
launchStationNote: For a station, this is the launch of the base object with this NORAD ID. Other modules may have launched separately.
launchOriginNote: These details refer to the original COSPAR launch. Spacecraft deployment or debris creation may have occurred later.
heroSub: Stations, bright, scientific, weather and navigation satellites on one map. Explore orbits in 3D, select objects and add more catalogs.
defaultHint: Start with stations, bright, scientific, weather and navigation satellites. Find more catalogs under All groups, or restore this selection with Recommended.
mapHint: Select an object to see its details. Open 3D to rotate Earth and inspect orbits from different angles.
debrisSub: The map shows objects with known orbits. Most small fragments cannot be displayed individually: their population is estimated using models.
statsError: ESA statistics could not be loaded.
statsTrackedNote: Satellites, stations, rocket bodies and debris.
statsEstimate: ESA model estimate. Individual orbits are mostly unknown.
statsMassNote: Mass of all space objects, including operational spacecraft.
statsContext: Collisions and breakups create new fragments. The dots on the map do not represent the entire debris population in orbit.
reentriesSub: Recorded orbital decays over the last 60 days. This is CelesTrak catalog history, not a prediction of impact locations or times.
reentriesError: CelesTrak is temporarily unavailable. The orbital decay list could not be retrieved.
guideSelectionBody: The selection covers different missions and orbital heights. Enable large constellations such as Starlink, debris and rocket bodies separately. Objects belonging to several groups appear only once.
guidePositionBody: SGP4 recalculates positions every 2 seconds using CelesTrak orbital elements, cached for 2 hours. These are calculated positions rather than GPS telemetry; check the orbital epoch in the object details.
guideCoverageBody: Open 3D, zoom or search by name or NORAD number. Object details include altitude, speed and orbital parameters. All usable public orbits from enabled groups are included; classified and untracked objects are not shown.
elementsBody: Public CelesTrak OMM orbital elements preserve full precision and support new six-digit NORAD catalog numbers.
realtimeBody: Positions are recalculated every 2 seconds without server requests. Click an object for its coordinates, orbital parameters and original elements.
stale: Using the last saved orbital elements. The source is temporarily unavailable; accuracy may be reduced.
workerError: Orbit calculation could not start. Reload this page.
webglError: 3D is unavailable on this device. Use the 2D view.
scaleNote: Distances and Earth radius share one scale. Object markers are enlarged. Lighting is schematic. The orbit line predicts one revolution in Earth's current orientation.
dataNote: All objects in the selected public groups with usable OMM elements, without a display cap; deduplicated by NORAD ID. SGP4 positions update every 2 seconds; source data is cached for 2 hours. Untracked small debris and objects without public orbits are excluded.
hint3d: Drag to rotate · scroll / pinch to zoom · click an object
hint2d: Drag the map · zoom · click an object

typeDescriptions.satellite: Artificial satellites from the selected catalogs, including communications, navigation, Earth observation and scientific spacecraft.
typeDescriptions.station: Orbital stations and associated spacecraft in the stations catalog, including the ISS and the Chinese space station.
typeDescriptions.debris: Tracked fragments of spacecraft and rockets. Small debris without public orbital elements is not displayed.
typeDescriptions.rocket: Spent rocket stages and bodies left in orbit after delivering their payloads.
typeDescriptions.unknown: Objects that cannot be assigned to the other types using the available data. They are not necessarily debris.

groupDescriptions.iss: The International Space Station, a crewed orbital laboratory. This catalog contains only the ISS.
groupDescriptions.stations: CelesTrak's space stations catalog, including orbital stations and associated spacecraft.
groupDescriptions.starlink: Satellites in the Starlink constellation, designed to provide broadband internet access.
groupDescriptions.visual: A selection of bright satellites suitable for ground-based observation. Visibility depends on location, time and illumination.
groupDescriptions.weather: Meteorological satellites observing clouds, the atmosphere and weather phenomena.
groupDescriptions.goes: GOES-series geostationary satellites observing weather and the near-Earth environment.
groupDescriptions.gps: Operational GPS satellites providing positioning and precise time through the US navigation system.
groupDescriptions.geo: CelesTrak's geosynchronous group. Orbital periods are close to Earth's rotation period; not every orbit is perfectly geostationary.
groupDescriptions.amateur: Satellites supporting amateur radio communications and signal transmission experiments.
groupDescriptions.active: CelesTrak's general active-satellite catalog. It overlaps many specialized groups; duplicate objects are merged.
groupDescriptions.debris: Objects with DEB in their names: tracked fragments from different launches, breakups and collisions.
groupDescriptions.rocket-bodies: Objects with R/B in their names: spent rocket bodies and stages remaining in orbit.
groupDescriptions.recent: Objects launched in the last 30 days for which CelesTrak publishes orbital elements.
groupDescriptions.analyst: Analyst catalog objects with tracked orbits whose identity or association with a particular launch may be uncertain.
groupDescriptions.fengyun-debris: Tracked fragments of the destroyed FENGYUN 1C meteorological satellite.
groupDescriptions.iridium-debris: Tracked fragments of IRIDIUM 33 following its collision with COSMOS 2251.
groupDescriptions.cosmos-debris: Tracked fragments of COSMOS 2251 following its collision with IRIDIUM 33.
groupDescriptions.resource: Earth remote-sensing satellites observing the surface, natural resources and the environment.
groupDescriptions.sar: Synthetic aperture radar satellites. Radar images reveal the surface at night and through clouds.
groupDescriptions.sarsat: Search-and-rescue satellites helping detect and locate distress beacon signals.
groupDescriptions.dmc: Satellites monitoring natural and human-caused disasters and assessing their effects.
groupDescriptions.tdrss: TDRSS relay satellites providing communications between ground stations and spacecraft.
groupDescriptions.argos: ARGOS satellites collecting and relaying data from remote sensors and platforms.
groupDescriptions.planet: Planet satellites imaging Earth and observing changes on its surface.
groupDescriptions.spire: Spire satellites collecting atmospheric, maritime and aviation data.
groupDescriptions.oneweb: OneWeb constellation satellites providing broadband communications from low Earth orbit.
groupDescriptions.qianfan: Satellites in the Chinese Qianfan constellation, designed for broadband satellite communications.
groupDescriptions.hulianwang: Satellites in the Chinese Hulianwang Digui low Earth orbit communications constellation.
groupDescriptions.kuiper: Internet constellation satellites listed under the Kuiper group in CelesTrak.
groupDescriptions.intelsat: Intelsat network satellites supporting telecommunications, data transmission and broadcasting.
groupDescriptions.ses: SES satellites supporting telecommunications, data transmission and television broadcasting.
groupDescriptions.eutelsat: Eutelsat group satellites supporting communications, broadcasting and data transmission.
groupDescriptions.telesat: Telesat network satellites providing satellite communications services.
groupDescriptions.iridium: Iridium NEXT satellites supporting mobile voice and data communications.
groupDescriptions.orbcomm: ORBCOMM satellites supporting small data messages, equipment monitoring and Internet of Things applications.
groupDescriptions.globalstar: Globalstar satellites providing mobile satellite communications and data services.
groupDescriptions.satnogs: CelesTrak's SatNOGS satellite group, associated with the open network of ground stations for satellite observations.
groupDescriptions.x-comm: Experimental satellites testing space communications technologies.
groupDescriptions.other-comm: Other communications satellites collected in a separate CelesTrak group.
groupDescriptions.gnss: Global navigation satellites, including GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou. This group overlaps the individual system catalogs.
groupDescriptions.glonass: Operational GLONASS satellites providing satellite navigation and precise time.
groupDescriptions.galileo: Satellites in Galileo, the European global navigation system.
groupDescriptions.beidou: Satellites in BeiDou, the Chinese global navigation system.
groupDescriptions.sbas: Navigation augmentation satellites, including WAAS, EGNOS and MSAS, supplementing global navigation system signals.
groupDescriptions.science: Spacecraft for space and Earth science, including scientific measurements, observations and experiments.
groupDescriptions.geodetic: Geodetic satellites measuring Earth's shape, gravity field and the positions of points on its surface.
groupDescriptions.engineering: Engineering and technology spacecraft testing space systems and equipment.
groupDescriptions.education: Educational satellites and spacecraft from teaching and student space projects.
groupDescriptions.military: Military spacecraft with publicly available orbital elements. This group does not include classified orbits.
groupDescriptions.radar: Satellites and dedicated objects used to calibrate and test ground-based radars.
groupDescriptions.cubesat: Small satellites built to the modular CubeSat standard for scientific, educational and technology missions.
